facts.text: XGRS Gamma-Ray Spectrometer was deployed at Asteroid 433 Eros (South Pole) during NEAR Shoemaker at Eros in 2001.
Combined X-ray and Gamma-Ray Spectrometer mounted to detect characteristic fluorescent X-rays (magnesium, aluminum, silicon) and gamma-ray lines (iron, potassium, thorium) from Eros's surface.
Engineered specifically to operate in the harsh vacuum and extreme temperatures of the lunar environment.
Proved Eros never underwent melting or differentiation, meaning its minerals have remained virtually unchanged since condensing from the solar nebula 4.56 billion years ago.
Status: Remains preserved in the arid regolith at Asteroid 433 Eros (South Pole).
A permanent human and robotic monument celebrating space exploration on the Moon.
